timeline.current_model: TP53 encodes a tetrameric transcription factor (p53) that functions as a tumor suppressor by transactivating target genes involved in cell cycle arrest, apoptosis, DNA repair, senescence, and autophagy; its stability and activity are tightly regulated by Mdm2-mediated ubiquitination and proteasomal degradation, counteracted by deubiquitinases (USP10, USP11), post-translational modifications including phosphorylation (e.g., Ser46 by a p53DINP1-associated kinase, ATM-mediated), acetylation (at K120 by NAT10, at K382 enhanced by ING4/5 via p300), beta-hydroxybutyrylation (at K120/319/370 by CBP, attenuating activity), and sumoylation/neddylation; p53 binds DNA preferentially at nucleosome edges as a pioneer factor; it produces multiple isoforms (e.g., Delta133p53, p53beta) with distinct and sometimes opposing functions including dominant-negative inhibition and promotion of invasion via EMT; in senescence, p53 drives pericentromeric heterochromatin dismantling through downregulation of TRF2; and hotspot missense mutations in its DNA-binding domain cause loss of sequence-specific DNA binding, dominant-negative effects on wild-type p53, and neomorphic gain-of-function activities including altered iron metabolism, enhanced metastasis, and remodeling of the tumor secretome.
